alignments.note: Rule 70: the ASV writes no word for the correlative particle. A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement; that is not a correction.
Rule 9: subject pronoun rides with the verb.

The noun of tribunals is recast as the infinitival to judge with the supplied generic object things. Both words are this noun's: the ASV's gloss note (Greek tribunals pertaining to) maps things onto the noun and pertaining to onto the adjective, and 1CO.6.2 renders the same noun to judge the … matters. Rule 58's reasoning keeps a supplied nominal with the expressed noun rather than with the attributive adjective beside it, and rule 66 heads on judge, things being the generic completion.

Attributive adjective rendered pertaining to this life. Rule 17's generic-noun clause is scoped to a substantival adjective and does not reach this one, κριτήρια standing expressed, so the supplied things belongs to that noun; 1CO.6.3, where the same adjective is substantival and no noun stands, keeps things in its own unit under that clause. Rule 66 heads on life, the word glossing the lexeme.

Interrogative auxiliary and subject ride with the verb under rule 9, and the supplied complement to judge completes what the seating verb says; discontinuous under rule 15. Rule 103's test is licensing and not recurrence, so this second to judge is a helper on καθίζετε and not added.
Rule 90: substantival article before a participle with one English word for the pair takes the relativizer.
Participle rendered by the copula plus of no account; rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing complement.

review_notes: Reading the clause as a question (ASV's main text) rather than the marginal imperative; the alignment is unaffected either way.

Reconciled with 1CO.6.2, the internal control: there the ASV gloss (Greek of the smallest tribunals) shows the supplied matters answering to κριτηρίων, and the same noun is recast as to judge in both verses.

1CO.6.3 is not touched by this: the adjective is substantival there, no noun is expressed, and it keeps things under rule 17's generic-noun clause. The presence of an expressed head noun is the test rules 22, 31, 47 and 58 already use.
Heads unchanged by the move: to judge things heads on judge under rule 66, matching 6:2, and pertaining to this life heads on life, matching 6:3.
